subject: chemistry

items.q: What happens to particles when a solid melts?
items.correct: They gain energy and can move past each other; their size is unchanged.
items.why: Changes of state alter particles' energy and arrangement, not their size or number.

items.q: Do the particles in a solid move?
items.correct: Yes — they vibrate about fixed positions.
items.random_wrong: They move around freely like a liquid.
items.why: Solid particles vibrate in place; they have energy but don't change places.

items.correct: Yes — a gas is just very spread out, so its density is low.
items.random_wrong: A gas is a continuous substance, not particles.
items.why: Gas particles do have mass; they are simply far apart.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620) syllabus; States of Matter
